plan: This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction with independent private values drawn uniformly from $0-$49. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do — it maximizes expected profit whether others bid truthfully, aggressively, or conservatively. Overbidding risks winning at a loss; underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $47, I will bid exactly my value to ensure optimal expected payoff, letting the second-price mechanism handle payment efficiently.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what others bid or believe, since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own. Overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. Since values are independently drawn and this is a one-shot game, the optimal strategy is straightforward: bid exactly my private value of $33, ensuring maximum expected profit.

This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction with 3 bidders, where bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy regardless of what others do. Since the winner pays the second-highest bid, there's no incentive to shade my bid below or above my true valuation of $36. Overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth to me; underbidding risks losing an item I'd profit from. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value.
